Cellular Automata

2026-11-22 7:59 PM

I think cellular automata (CAs) are neat. From simple rules you can get really complex behaviour, Turing-completeness, and somewhat realistic models of physical phenomena.

Other than Conway's Game of Life, some notable CAs are:

  • Langton's ant
  • Rule 30 (pseudorandom number generation)
  • Rule 110 (Turing-complete)
  • Wireworld (used to simulate logic circuits)

Think Complexity

This book has a lot of interesting simulations for complex systems, with Python programs using numpy and cross-correlation kernels. I am interested in implementing these 2D discrete models, mostly related to CAs.

  • Percolation cellular automaton
  • Drossel-Schwabl forest-fire model
  • Abelian sand pile model
  • Sugarscape (agent-based model)
    • This last one isn't actually a cellular automaton, but it looks cool.

Lattice Gas Automata

Recently I read about lattice-gas cellular automata, an early model for simulating fluid flows. I have spent the past couple days making a visualiser in Python: https://github.com/allanwupi/lattice-gas-automata. The results are very pretty!
